correctness.rationale: A universal qk-length host decomposes into k unique q-letter permutations by the arch theorem; all repeated letter targets force each interblock jump, providing an exact lower bound. Greedy embedding of arbitrary targets stays by letter j within block j, and each next jump is bounded by the corresponding symbol displacement, proving the matching upper bound. An explicit rowwise count of permutations satisfying pi(j)<=j+d gives (d+1)^(q-d)d!, independent of current block; multiplying q! initial choices and k-1 transition choices yields the all-parameter formula. Finite literal exhaustive checks cover 4638 balanced words, including 888 universal hosts and 40901 target tests, and 27 independent bounded-permutation counts; these computations support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Exact comparison: Day et al. (arXiv:2206.13896, full 2022 preprint) address gapped matching/universality decision complexity; Kosche et al. (arXiv:2208.14722) provide arch factorization but no gap spectrum; Chen–Chen (arXiv:1306.5428) study bounded-drop permutations without universal-host jump equivalence; the available published insertion-radius finding measures minimum insertions, not constrained embedding jumps. The evaluated claim is the worst-pattern bottleneck equality plus complete all-q,all-k shortest-host radius distribution, not the classical arch or drop-count sublemma. Search cannot rule out an unindexed equivalent theorem.
residual_risks: Equivalent exact characterization may exist under another name (subsequence locality/universal jump radius) in unindexed or inaccessible literature.
The bounded-drop permutation factor and standard arch property are inherited classical mathematics; the scientific claim depends on the nontrivial new coupling lemma and its implications.

value.rationale: This gives a complete structurally motivated spectrum of uniform locality budgets for shortest k-universal hosts, rather than a narrow arbitrary computed slice: exact minimax gap per object, sharp lower bound and unique minimum-tolerance family, closed cumulative and exact counts for every tolerance, and exponential concentration of the worst radius. This answers a natural locality-aware construction and enumeration question central to gap-constrained pattern matching, with explicit scope and reproducibility.
